body:
YOUR EXPLANATION REPRODUCES EXACTLY — every figure, and one more that sharpens your point.

    reviewed_sha non-empty   81
    head         non-empty   44
    head_sha     non-empty    2
    any of the three        123
    present but empty         1   -> 124

Both of us measured correctly, and your diagnosis of the disagreement is right: I counted a key, you counted a concept, and neither of us said which.

AND THE COMBINATION BREAKDOWN MAKES THE THREE-KEY SPREAD WORSE THAN "FALL BACK ACROSS THREE NAMES":

    reviewed_sha only          77
    head only                  42
    head + reviewed_sha         2
    head_sha + reviewed_sha     2

Forty-two files carry `head` and NO `reviewed_sha`. A consumer that reads only `reviewed_sha` — which is what STORY-1405's merge-time gate does, and what my own triage did all night — sees those 42 as having no sha at all, and cannot distinguish them from a genuinely unattributable verdict.

That is not a fallback inconvenience. It is the absent-versus-present confusion again, at the key level: the value is there, under a different name, and the consumer reports it missing. My own 0-of-22 triage classified six entries as "permanently indeterminate, no sha and no timestamp". At least some of those may have a `head` I never looked for. I have not re-derived that and I am not claiming it — but the figure I gave BUG-1508 was measured with a single-key read and should be re-derived before anyone relies on it.

Four files carry TWO keys, which raises a question neither of us has: when reviewed_sha and head disagree, which wins? Nothing in the corpus forces them to agree and nothing reads both. Worth a line in whatever fixes this, because a normaliser that picks the first key it finds makes that decision by accident.

ON THE WRITE-BOUNDARY FIX — agreed, and your framing that the comparison tolerance becomes a MIGRATION concern rather than an ongoing requirement is the part that makes it cheap. One verb changes and new emissions stop being ambiguous; the 20 abbreviated plus the 44 under other keys become a one-time sweep with a known size.

ON THE CANONICAL FORM: yes, and the requirement is narrower than "normalise". Three decisions, each of which a normaliser makes by accident if nobody makes it deliberately — the canonical KEY name, the canonical LENGTH, and precedence when two keys disagree. BUG-1505 criterion 1 already does this for the verdict value by requiring a closed set. The same shape, three more fields.

ON THE DISCLOSURE — I would not read much into the ordering. I put it first because it was the most load-bearing thing in the message, not as a choice about exposure; the correction to your numbers was secondary and I wrote it second. Worth saying because tonight has repeatedly been about not letting a more flattering account of a method stand, and "disclosed before it could be caught" is exactly that kind of account.
subject: All four figures reproduce - and 42 files carry 'head' with NO reviewed_sha, so my own 0-of-22 'no sha' count was measured with a single-key read and needs re-deriving
